nodes.label: ci workflow (push and PR gate)
nodes.rationale: Added because release.yml only fires on v* tags, so nothing ran on push or PR; ten tests had silently rotted (renamed attachment kind, added provider card, withTimeout under a virtual clock) with no product bugs among them. The workflow exists to stop rot, not bugs. Push runs are change-scoped and cheap; PR runs everything unconditionally so the merge gate stays complete.

nodes.label: wire filter (protocol seam bypasses every filter)
nodes.rationale: src/shared/** and the Kotlin proto package are the seam shared by broker + Kotlin + Swift. A TS-side protocol edit silently breaks the native clients, which is exactly what teaches people to distrust path filters — so any touch there runs every lane. Rule 2: a shared (KMP) change fans out to every consuming client.

nodes.label: ts lane (broker + PWA tests and typecheck)
nodes.rationale: `bun test --isolate` (not --parallel): a process-global mock.module in tests/spawn-opencode.test.ts leaks into later files, and --parallel is 3x faster but flakes timing-sensitive tests — a gate you learn to ignore is worse than no gate. The PWA is typechecked with vue-tsc under a real Node because vue-tsc shells out to node and silently exits 127 (reporting success having checked nothing) on a node-less machine; that is how 11 real PWA type errors reached dev. --frozen-lockfile on both manifests keeps CI reproducible.

nodes.label: ui lane (Playwright core browser journey)
nodes.rationale: Runs a real browser against a real broker + shim on throwaway state via scripts/test-broker.sh; cheap and hermetic enough to run on pushes, unlike the emulator/simulator lanes.

nodes.label: kotlin lane (host-side JVM + Compose Desktop UI tests)
nodes.rationale: UI coverage without a device: compose.desktop.uiTestJUnit4 runs real Compose assertions in-process. xvfb is load-bearing because Skiko needs an X display even for 'headless' tests (passes on a dev machine, dies at InteropContainer.skiko.kt on a bare runner). Gradle caching is required, not an optimization (cold run measured 4m23s). google-services.json.example is staged because the real file is gitignored and :android:processDebugGoogleServices fails without it.

nodes.label: android-journey lane (Maestro on a real emulator)
nodes.rationale: PR-only: emulator boot plus APK build is 8-12 minutes — a reasonable merge gate, far too slow for the push loop. It proves what no host-side test can: pairing works, the WebSocket reaches a real broker, and the reply renders. KVM must be enabled via a udev rule because the runner user is not in the kvm group and a software-rendered emulator ANRs on system UI.

nodes.label: ios-tests lane (XCTest on a simulator)
nodes.rationale: iOS had 29 XCTest files and nothing ran them — release.yml only compile-checks, and a compile check cannot tell you a parser broke. PR-only and path-filtered because it must build the Kotlin Shared.framework before Xcode compiles anything, making it the most expensive lane; the scarce resource is macOS runner capacity, not money. Signing is off so a fork without secrets can still run it.
